standard.title: Identification of Parts for Complete, Filled Transport Packages when Testing (First Revision)
standard.sector: Transport Engineering / Transport Packaging and Pallets
standard.description: This standard specifies a standardized, uniform system for identifying the different parts (surfaces, edges, and corners) of complete, filled transport packages when undergoing mechanical, physical, or environmental testing. It covers parallelepipedal (box-shaped) packages, cylindrical packages, sacks and bags, and miscellaneous packages.
standard.scope: This standard specifies a standardized, uniform system for identifying the different parts (surfaces, edges, and corners) of complete, filled transport packages when undergoing mechanical, physical, or environmental testing. certification.description: Voluntary Procedural Standard (Transport Packaging). Since IS 7030 is an engineering methodology code rather than a consumer product, it is certified on a voluntary basis under BIS schemes. However, compliance with its structural designs, material thickness categories, air-tight joints, vaned grids, and support brackets is universally mandated inside all national public, defense, Indian Navy, port authority, and commercial shipyard procurement contracts to ensure air-tightness and corrosion protection.
requirements: Requires placing the package in its intended transport position. If unknown, arbitrarily select one. If a manufacturer's joint exists, it must be placed vertically on the observer's right. With one side facing the observer, identify surfaces as: No. 1 (Top), No. 2 (Right), No. 3 (Bottom), No. 4 (Left), No. 5 (Nearest / Front), and No. 6 (Farthest away / Rear). If more than one manufacturer's joint exists, arbitrarily select one end as No. 5.
Edges are designated by combining the numbers of the two meeting surfaces. For example, edge '1-2' identifies the line formed by the meeting of the top surface (No. 1) and the right surface (No. 2).
Corners are designated by combining the numbers of the three meeting surfaces. For example, corner '1-2-5' identifies the point where the top (No. 1), right (No. 2), and front (No. 5) surfaces meet.

The ends of two perpendicular diameters on the upper surface of the cylinder are designated as 1, 3, 5, and 7. The corresponding parallel lines along the cylinder axis are designated as 2, 4, 6, and 8 respectively. The axial lines connecting them are designated as lines 1-2, 3-4, 5-6, and 7-8. If a manufacturer's joint exists, it should occupy the position 5-6.

The sack or bag is placed flat on one face with its sealed/bottom end towards the observer. Any side seam must be positioned on the observer's right. If two side seams exist, one must be on the right and the other on the left. If a longitudinal seam exists, it must face downwards, with the top (filling end) of the sack pointing away from the observer. Surfaces are then identified systematically starting from the uppermost face.

Irregularly shaped packages must be arbitrarily mapped using analogous designations derived from the basic parallelepipedal or cylindrical models, with all reference numbers and selected orientations fully documented in the testing report.
